title: Ang 558–574: the Gurus in Vadhans
tomorrow: why would a scripture sing about a wedding horse?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Vadhans: the addict, the fish, and the lover of God who finds everyone dear. Today, a look at whether that held up at a real table.

The best part of any community dinner is the end, when people who didn't know each other are stacking chairs side by side. Here's how heritage night went, from Simran's texts. The rotis ran out early. Maya served all night. And the boy from the bus sat on the floor next to her cousin, eating dal. Side by side. Nobody planned that part. The Gurus in Vadhans sing of a deeper meeting, and its word is union.
screen: `STACKING CHAIRS SIDE BY SIDE.` → `HERITAGE NIGHT.` → `NOBODY PLANNED THAT PART.`

segments.voice: These pages of Vadhans belong to the Gurus: Guru Amar Das, Guru Ram Das, then Guru Arjan, hymns of union and longing. Union here is the soul meeting the Lord, the bride's long night finally answered. And Guru Amar Das starts with where that meeting can't happen. In paraphrase: with a dirty mind, everything is dirty; washing the body doesn't make the mind clean. You've heard that shape before: Farid's inside matching the outside, Guru Nanak's grinding stone inside you. Then Guru Ram Das sings the hope out loud. In paraphrase: in my mind is a great hope; how will I meet the Lord? That's two weeks, really. Look back. Sandalwood. From the heart. Gentle. The passing world. Night longing. Longing songs. Mardana's two cups. And Vadhans, where everyone is dear. A longing, all the way through, and at the end a table where a farmer's list of names, a Sufi's heart, a neighbor's Shema and a letter of John all had a seat. Union.
screen: `THE GURUS IN VADHANS.` · `A DIRTY MIND, A WASHED BODY.` · `A GREAT HOPE: HOW WILL I MEET HIM?` · `TWO WEEKS, ONE LONGING.` · then, large: `UNION.`

segments.voice: Say these out loud, slowly, one breath each: sandalwood, from the heart, gentle, the passing world, night longing, vadhans. Then rest on the last word, union, for the sit. If you'd like, read a hymn on ang 560 first.
Ang 558. Where the Gurus' hymns in Vadhans begin, with Guru Amar Das on the mind that washing can't clean.
Union: the longing of the night songs, finally meeting what it longed for. Next week, a wedding party.
